text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. In senior news management it's unfortunately common, and panels can pick women or men on merit. Treated as your headline argument, it looks speculative and puts the employer on the defensive.

It is, however, a legitimate procedural criticism — many public broadcasters have their own diversity guidance on panel composition, and failing to follow it is worth noting as one factor among several.

Your stronger points: the unanswered request for written reasons (chase it, in writing, with a deadline), whether "strong experience of digital media" appeared in the published person specification, and how experience was weighted against it.

Push on process and criteria. Mention the panel; don't lead with it.
